clue.text: Lesser runner, a male regularly getting in the way

indicators.note: getting in tells us the short group of letters goes inside the road word

parts.note: a way is a road, a street

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word male, starting with its first

explanation.surface: A man loitering in the road blocks a smaller athlete's path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes M and L from 'male'; with A in front, AML goes inside STREET.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner can be a watercourse, and a small stream is lesser than a river.

clue.text: Daughter occupying position on first of ensembles composed

indicators.note: occupying means the daughter's letter sits within the position word

parts.note: a seat is a position, as in a seat on a committee

indicators.note: first of takes just the opening letter of ensembles

explanation.surface: A girl takes her place at the front of a group of musicians, all calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply puts the E after SEDAT in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Composed and sedate are synonyms, both describing someone calm and unruffled.

clue.text: Parties ending in clover pause to recollect outstanding victory

indicators.note: ending in picks out the final letter of the word clover
read as re-collect, gathering the letters together again in a new order

parts.note: V is the familiar sign and abbreviation for victory

explanation.surface: Someone at a party in the clover stops to remember a great win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to recollect' is read as re-collect, gathering letters together anew; 'outstanding victory' suggests a triumph but is the V-for-victory sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Rave-ups are lively, noisy parties in informal British usage.

clue.text: 6 Down in musicals, optional

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the phrase musicals, optional

explanation.surface: A conductor's role in stage shows is merely optional.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 Down is CONDUCTOR; Marin Alsop is an American conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Marin Alsop is a celebrated American orchestral conductor, an example of the type.

clue.text: Current controller, one quick to check your ticket?

definitions.meaning: a metal rod that carries electrical discharge from a strike safely to earth

definitions.text: one quick to check your ticket?
definitions.meaning: a very speedy bus or train official who inspects fares

explanation.surface: An electrical device is also a ticket inspector who works at speed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: lightning means very fast, and a bus or train conductor checks tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod fitted to buildings channels the electric current of a strike into the ground, controlling it.

clue.text: 6 Down more than half way through opera

indicators.note: stopping more than half way through the name means its last letters are cut off

parts.note: Arturo Toscanini, the great Italian conductor

explanation.surface: A conductor is past the midpoint of a performance of an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 Down is CONDUCTOR; the first five of TOSCANINI's nine letters remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's Tosca is a famous Italian opera.

clue.text: Queens, say, adopting small sheds

indicators.note: adopting means taking the small letter in, inside the queens word

parts.note: a queen is a female cat, so queens are examples of cats

explanation.surface: Royal women take in something little and throw things off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queens' suggests royalty, but a queen is a female cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake casts or sheds its skin; the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: See 4
Difference between three points is set

indicators.note: between puts the quarrel word among the three compass letters

parts.note: S, E and N are three points of the compass
a tiff is a small quarrel, a difference of opinion

explanation.surface: A disagreement in a game score of three points is settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' places the quarrel among compass points; 'Difference' looks like arithmetic but means a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jelly or concrete that sets becomes firm, which is to stiffen.

clue.text: Female put on ring turned over in varnish

indicators.note: in a down answer, put on places the female word on top of the rest

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: turned over says the ring word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them

explanation.surface: A woman puts on a ring that has been flipped, within a coat of varnish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' reverses CALL to LLAC beneath SHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac is a resin used to make a glossy varnish for wood.

clue.text: 6 Down, his supporter welcoming Beethoven's Seventh

indicators.note: welcoming means the platform word takes the letter inside it

parts.note: a dais is a raised platform that supports a speaker or conductor

indicators.note: Seventh picks the seventh letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A conductor's backer warmly receives Beethoven's Seventh Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's Seventh' sounds like the symphony, but it is the seventh letter, V. 6 Down is CONDUCTOR: Sir Colin Davis.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Colin Davis was a leading British orchestral conductor, an example of the type.

clue.text: Wheel engages in fuel-driven machine

indicators.note: to wheel is to turn round, so these letters are spun into a new order

explanation.surface: A wheel engages within a petrol-powered machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wheel' looks like a part of the machine but it is a verb telling us to turn the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas engine is an internal combustion engine running on gaseous fuel.

clue.text: Time to carry blow

parts.note: to hump is to carry something heavy, in British informal usage

explanation.surface: It's time to take the strain of a hard knock.
explanation.walkthrough: HUMP, meaning to lug a load, is everyday British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A thump is a heavy blow or punch.

clue.text: Fix faucet up, having leaked originally about 5 fluid ounces

indicators.note: fix is read as rearrange, putting these letters right in a new order
originally takes the first letter of leaked

explanation.surface: Repair the tap since it dripped roughly a cup of water at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' looks like plumbing, but it rearranges FAUCETUP plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup holds roughly five fluid ounces, so that quantity is a cupful of tea.

clue.text: Three consecutive notes lacking a 6 Down

indicators.note: lacking means the letter a is dropped from the notes

parts.note: so, la and ti follow one another in the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A conductor is missing three notes in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 Down is CONDUCTOR: Sir Georg Solti.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Georg Solti was a renowned Hungarian-British conductor, an example of the type.

clue.text: Male in mobile toilet providing theme

indicators.note: in places the male letter inside the jumbled letters
mobile means moving, so the letters move into a new order

parts.note: providing means if, as in providing it rains

explanation.surface: A man in a portable loo supplies a recurring motif.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' rearranges the loo to LEITOT, and 'in' places the male letter inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotif is a recurring musical theme linked to a character or idea.

clue.text: An act is horribly evil

indicators.note: horribly suggests the letters are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An act is dreadfully wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means devilish, utterly wicked.

clue.text: Extra fat needed after a blowout?

definitions.meaning: a roll of excess flesh round the waist
the extra wheel you fit when a tyre bursts

explanation.surface: Excess weight piles on after a feast, or a car needs a spare after a burst tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: A blowout is both a big meal and a tyre bursting.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a spare wheel and a bulge of fat round the middle.

clue.text: Splendid having a slash?

definitions.meaning: excellent, great, in old-fashioned British slang
taken literally, making a tear or cut

explanation.walkthrough: 'Slash' is also British slang for urinating, a further misleading sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripping is dated British slang for excellent, and also means tearing.

clue.text: Chefs' instructions to serve up classic cuisine, ultimately, in empty restaurants

indicators.note: in puts the turned letters within the remains of the empty restaurants
empty removes everything but the outer letters of restaurants
in a down answer, serving up sends the letters upwards, reversed

parts.note: a classic or epic work is a monumental one

indicators.note: ultimately takes the last letter of cuisine

explanation.surface: Cooking directions for dishing up fine food in deserted eateries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to serve up' reverses EPICE to ECIPE, which sits between R and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Recipes are the written directions a cook follows to make a dish.

clue.text: Go on piano with 6 Down

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
Sir Simon Rattle, the British conductor

explanation.surface: Carry on at the piano with the conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 Down is CONDUCTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on, in the sense of talking at length, is to prattle or chatter.

clue.text: Drier river taking last of water

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire, England

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of water

explanation.surface: A river with less water becomes drier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drier' looks like a comparative adjective, but it is a noun: a thing that dries.
explanation.definitionFit: An airer is a rack on which washing is hung to dry, so it is a drier.

clue.text: Girls' school dismissing an Elizabeth, elegant beast

indicators.note: dismissing means the word an is sent out of the school name

parts.note: Roedean is a well-known English girls' boarding school
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A girls' school expels a pupil named Elizabeth, a graceful creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Roedean is a famous independent girls' school near Brighton; ER is the Queen's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe deer is a small, graceful Eurasian deer.

clue.text: 6 Down stands to embrace new song

indicators.note: to embrace means the reversed name holds the new letter
in a down answer, standing upright reads the name from bottom to top

parts.note: Zubin Mehta, the Indian conductor

explanation.surface: A conductor rises to hug a fresh tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stands' reverses MEHTA to ATHEM, and N goes after A. 6 Down is CONDUCTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a song, especially a solemn or rousing one.

clue.text: Message about redirected mail can be taken

indicators.note: about means the message word goes around the jumbled letters

parts.note: a cable is a telegram, a message

indicators.note: redirected mail is sent another way, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A note about forwarded post can be collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redirected' rearranges the post into a new order, and 'about' wraps the telegram word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something claimable may be rightly taken or demanded as one's own.

clue.text: Reported 4 6

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the answer is a word heard rather than written

parts.note: 4 Down is lightning, and a bolt is a flash of lightning

explanation.surface: Bare cross-references: a word sounding like a strike, naming a conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is CONDUCTOR: Sir Adrian Boult, the English conductor; his name sounds like a bolt of lightning.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Adrian Boult was a leading English conductor, an example of the type.

clue.text: 6 Down abandoning European capital, the mug!

indicators.note: abandoning means the capital's letters are left out of the name

parts.note: Leonard Bernstein, the American conductor and composer
Bern is the capital of Switzerland

explanation.surface: A conductor leaves a European capital, the fool!
explanation.walkthrough: 'the mug!' sounds like an insult, but the mug is a beer tankard. 6 Down is CONDUCTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A stein is a large earthenware beer mug, from German.

clue.text: Blade turned up in wastepaper basket

indicators.note: turned up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sword, flipped over, sits inside a bin.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden letters sit across 'wastepaper basket' and nothing names the hiding, only 'in' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabre is a sword with a curved blade.

clue.text: Panel shaken up and jittery

indicators.note: shaken means the letters are jumbled about

explanation.surface: A jury, rattled and nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is 'up' and 'jittery'; 'and' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A petit jury is the ordinary trial jury, a panel of twelve, as opposed to a grand jury.

clue.text: Wood — 6 Down leaving in the morning

indicators.note: leaving means the morning letters depart from the name

parts.note: Sir Thomas Beecham, the English conductor
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

explanation.surface: A conductor goes off to the forest early in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 Down is CONDUCTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Beech is the timber of the beech tree, so it is a type of wood.

clue.text: Supporter starts to show honest spirit

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letters of show and honest

parts.note: an elf is a small supernatural spirit

explanation.surface: Something that begins to reveal a genuine spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelf is a ledge that holds books and objects up, a support.

clue.text: The judge ruling on misdemeanour initially coming out of that place

parts.note: a referee, or ref, judges a match

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of ruling, on and misdemeanour

explanation.surface: A referee rules on a foul in the first instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefrom is a formal adverb meaning from that source or location.
